raw_segments.text: If it be supposed that amongst the states which are united by the federal tie, there
are some which exclusively enjoy the principal advantages of union, or whose prosperity depends
on the duration of that union, it is unquestionable that they will always be ready to support
the central government in enforcing the obedience of the others.
But the government would then be exerting a force not derived from itself, but from
a principal contrary to its nature.
States form confederations in order to derive equal advantages from their union, and in
the case just alluded to, the federal government would derive its power from the unequal distribution
of those benefits amongst the states.
